instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Aromatics
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. In a large pot, melt 1 tablespoon of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Build the Base
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to deepen its flavor. Sprinkle in the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring to create a light roux. This helps thicken the soup slightly.

instructions.title: Add Liquids and Simmer
instructions.text: Gradually pour in the vegetable or chicken broth, whisking constantly to prevent lumps. Add the rinsed red lentils, salt, and black pepper. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender.

instructions.title: Blend the Soup
instructions.text: Once the lentils are tender, remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup until it is smooth and creamy. If you do not have an immersion blender, transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return it to the pot. Adjust consistency with a little more hot water or broth if desired.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chili-Mint Butter
instructions.text: In a small saucepan, melt the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter over low heat. Add the dried mint and red pepper flakes. Cook for about 30 seconds, stirring constantly, until the spices are fragrant. Be careful not to burn the butter or spices.

instructions.title: Serve Mercimek Corbasi
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle each serving with a spoonful of the chili-mint butter. Garnish with fresh chopped mint or parsley, and serve immediately with lemon wedges on the side for squeezing. The lemon brightens the flavors beautifully.

tips: Always rinse your red lentils thoroughly to remove any impurities and ensure a clear, vibrant soup base.
For an extra layer of flavor, consider adding a small diced carrot and potato along with the onion and garlic at the beginning of cooking.
Serve Mercimek Corbasi piping hot with a generous squeeze of fresh lemon juice; it truly elevates the soup's taste.
article:
Turkish cuisine is a vibrant tapestry of flavors, deeply rooted in history and tradition. From aromatic kebabs to sweet baklava, each dish tells a story. Among the many culinary treasures, soups hold a special place, often served at every meal, even breakfast. They are the heart of Turkish hospitality, offering warmth, comfort, and nourishment. While there are countless varieties, one stands out as a universally beloved classic: Mercimek Corbasi. This simple yet profoundly flavorful red lentil soup is a staple in every Turkish home and restaurant, cherished for its smooth texture, wholesome ingredients, and invigorating taste. Whether you're seeking a hearty start to your day, a light lunch, or a comforting dinner, Mercimek Corbasi is an experience that promises to delight your palate and warm your soul.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi (Turkish Red Lentil Soup)?

Mercimek Corbasi, pronounced "mer-jee-mek chor-ba-suh," is much more than just a soup; it's an institution in Turkey. This iconic red lentil soup embodies the essence of Turkish comfort food – simple, nutritious, and incredibly satisfying. Originating from Anatolian kitchens, it has become a national favorite, enjoyed by people of all ages across the country. The soup is characterized by its brilliant orange-red hue and velvety smooth texture, achieved by blending cooked lentils and vegetables until creamy.

At its core, Mercimek Corbasi is a testament to the power of humble ingredients. Red lentils, the star of the show, are simmered with a base of sautéed onions, carrots, and often potatoes, infused with a touch of tomato paste and traditional spices. What truly elevates this soup, however, is the final drizzle of *nane yağı* – a sizzling butter infused with dried mint and vibrant red pepper flakes. This aromatic topping adds an indispensable layer of flavor and a beautiful visual flourish, transforming a simple lentil soup into something extraordinary. Beyond its delicious taste, Mercimek Corbasi is celebrated for its health benefits. Rich in protein, fiber, and essential nutrients, it's a wonderfully wholesome and naturally vegetarian dish that provides sustained energy and comfort, making it a perfect choice any time of year.

## Ingredients for Mercimek Corbasi

The beauty of Mercimek Corbasi lies in its straightforward ingredients, many of which you likely already have in your pantry. Using fresh, good-quality components will ensure the most authentic and flavorful result.

For the Soup Base:
*   **Red Lentils:** Approximately 1 cup (200g) of dried red lentils. These cook quickly and break down easily, contributing to the soup's signature smoothness.
*   **Onion:** 1 medium onion, finely chopped. Provides an aromatic foundation.
*   **Carrot:** 1 medium carrot, finely chopped or grated. Adds natural sweetness and depth.
*   **Potato (Optional but Recommended):** 1 small potato, peeled and diced. Contributes to the creamy texture and heartiness.
*   **Garlic (Optional):** 1-2 cloves, minced. Enhances the overall savory profile.
*   **Tomato Paste (Salça):** 1-2 tablespoons. A crucial ingredient for color and a rich umami flavor.
*   **Flour (Optional):** 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour. Used to lightly thicken the soup and create a roux with the oil/butter, though many modern recipes omit it for a lighter touch.
*   **Water or Vegetable Broth:** 6-8 cups (1.5-2 liters). The liquid base for cooking the lentils and vegetables. Broth adds more flavor.
*   **Salt and Black Pepper:** To taste.
*   **Olive Oil or Butter:** 2-3 tablespoons for sautéing.

For the Mint & Pepper Infused Butter (Nane Yağı - Crucial Topping):
*   **Butter:** 2 tablespoons. Unsalted butter is traditional and provides a rich flavor.
*   **Dried Mint (Kuru Nane):** 1-2 teaspoons. Essential for the distinctive Turkish aroma.
*   **Red Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber or Maras Biber):** 1-2 teaspoons, or to taste. Provides a mild warmth and vibrant color.

Optional Garnish:
*   Fresh lemon wedges
*   Fresh mint leaves, chopped

## How to Make Mercimek Corbasi: Step-by-Step

Creating a delicious pot of Mercimek Corbasi is surprisingly simple, requiring minimal fuss for maximum flavor. Follow these steps for an authentic experience:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any dust or debris. Drain well.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil or butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add the chopped carrot (and potato, if using) and minced garlic (if using), and continue to cook for another 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
3.  **Build the Flavor Base:** Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to deepen its flavor and color. If using flour, sprinkle it over the vegetables and tomato paste, stirring constantly for another minute to cook out the raw flour taste.
4.  **Add Lentils and Liquid:** Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot. Pour in the water or vegetable broth. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Bring the mixture to a boil.
5.  **Simmer and Cook:** Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are very tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
6.  **Blend Until Smooth:** Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it is completely smooth and creamy. Alternatively, you can transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender (be cautious with hot liquids – fill only halfway and vent the lid) and blend until smooth, then return it to the pot.
7.  **Adjust Consistency and Seasoning:** If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired consistency. Taste and adjust salt and pepper if needed. Gently reheat the soup over low heat.
8.  **Prepare the Nane Yağı (Mint & Pepper Butter):** While the soup is reheating or just before serving, melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Once melted, remove from heat and stir in the dried mint and red pepper flakes. The heat from the butter will gently toast the spices, releasing their aroma. Be careful not to burn them.
9.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle a spoonful of the aromatic *nane yağı* over each serving. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side.

## Tips for the Best Turkish Red Lentil Soup

Achieving the perfect bowl of Mercimek Corbasi is easy with a few key tips:

*   **Rinse Lentils Thoroughly:** This is crucial to remove any impurities and starch, which can make the soup cloudy.
*   **Don't Skimp on the Sautéing:** Allowing the onions, carrots, and tomato paste to sauté properly develops their flavors and creates a richer base for the soup. The slight caramelization adds depth.
*   **Quality Tomato Paste:** Turkish tomato paste (salça) is known for its intense flavor. Using a good quality paste will significantly impact the soup's taste and color.
*   **Blend Until Velvety Smooth:** The characteristic texture of Mercimek Corbasi is incredibly smooth. An immersion blender makes this task effortless. If using a regular blender, ensure no chunks remain. For an extra silken texture, you can even pass the blended soup through a fine-mesh sieve, though this is rarely necessary.
*   **Adjust Consistency:** Red lentils absorb a lot of liquid. Don't hesitate to add more hot water or broth during or after blending if the soup becomes too thick for your liking. It should be thick enough to coat a spoon, but still pourable.
*   **The *Nane Yağı* is Non-Negotiable:** This mint and pepper infused butter is what truly defines Mercimek Corbasi. Do not skip it! The sizzling butter gently toasts the dried mint and chili flakes, releasing their full aromatic potential and adding a beautiful finish.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** Always taste your soup before serving and adjust the seasoning. A squeeze of fresh lemon juice at the end can brighten all the flavors.

## Serving Suggestions for Mercimek Corbasi

Mercimek Corbasi is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways throughout the day. Its comforting nature makes it suitable for various occasions.

*   **With a Squeeze of Lemon:** This is the most traditional accompaniment. A fresh lemon wedge is always served alongside, allowing each diner to add a bright, tangy counterpoint that cuts through the richness of the lentils and butter.
*   **Crusty Bread (Pide or Simit):** A staple in Turkish meals, crusty bread like freshly baked *pide* or a sesame-crusted *simit* is perfect for dipping into the soup, soaking up all its delicious flavors.
*   **Pickles (Turşu):** A small side dish of Turkish mixed pickles (turşu) offers a wonderful tart crunch that complements the creamy soup beautifully.
*   **Green Salad:** For a lighter meal, Mercimek Corbasi pairs wonderfully with a simple, crisp green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon juice.
*   **Yogurt (Optional):** While not always traditional for red lentil soup, a dollop of plain yogurt can be swirled in for an extra layer of creaminess and tang, especially if you enjoy a slightly milder flavor.
*   **Breakfast, Lunch, or Dinner:** In Turkey, soup is often eaten at all three meals. Mercimek Corbasi is hearty enough for a light breakfast, perfect for a warming lunch, and a comforting starter or main course for dinner.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Mercimek Corbasi recipe is perfect as is, there are a few ways you can adapt it to your taste or dietary needs:

*   **Spices:** Some variations include a pinch of cumin or sweet paprika in the soup base for an extra layer of warmth and earthy flavor. You can also adjust the amount of red pepper flakes in the *nane yağı* to control the level of heat.
*   **Vegetables:** Feel free to add other finely diced vegetables like celery or a small amount of bell pepper alongside the carrots and onions for added nutrients and complexity. A small amount of finely chopped fresh tomatoes can also be added with the tomato paste.
*   **Broth Alternatives:** While water or vegetable broth are common, chicken or beef broth can be used for a richer, meatier flavor, though this would change the soup from being vegetarian.
*   **Vegan Option:** To make Mercimek Corbasi completely vegan, ensure you use vegetable broth (or water) and substitute the butter in the *nane yağı* with olive oil. The flavor will still be fantastic.
*   **Heartier Soup:** For a thicker, more substantial soup, some cooks add a tablespoon or two of fine bulgur or rice along with the lentils. This will make the soup less smooth and more stew-like, but it's a popular variation in some regions.
*   **Fresh Herbs:** While dried mint is traditional for the topping, a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley or dill can be added to the soup just before serving for a burst of freshness.

Mercimek Corbasi is more than just a dish; it's a culinary hug in a bowl, a testament to the comforting power of simple, wholesome ingredients. Its vibrant color, silky texture, and deeply satisfying flavor make it a beloved staple that transcends cultural boundaries. Whether you're exploring Turkish cuisine for the first time or looking to recreate a cherished memory, making this iconic red lentil soup is a rewarding experience. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to be enchanted by the timeless allure of Turkish Mercimek Corbasi. It’s a soup that truly nourishes both body and soul.
